segments.text: Welcome to the Robotics Digest for October 16th, 2026.
We're diving into Skild AI's latest, evolving robot bodies, and fascinating insights on robot cognition.
Today, we cover two big stories.

From thesequence.substack.com, The Sequence Robotics - Issue number nine hundred fifty two details Skild AI's research into transferring robotic intelligence across different hardware rather than requiring complete rebuilds for each machine, focusing on motor adaptation, video-prompted task learning, and self-play.

The research centers on separating intelligence from the physical body so that the model learns how to inhabit various physical forms by learning what a body is, rather than depending on perfect prior engineering specifications.

The methodology involves training the model to achieve this transferability through these processes, though the challenge involves testing whether these capabilities can meet real-world demands for speed, reliability, and safety in deployment.
This approach investigates the model's ability to learn physical embodiment through experience.
The findings suggest a path toward more flexible and adaptable artificial intelligence systems capable of operating across diverse robotic platforms.
From Robohub, Robot Talk Episode 166 – Evolving robot bodies and brains, with Rika Antonova.
This segment explores the use of artificial intelligence to develop complementary robot hardware and algorithms through co-design and automated discovery processes.
Rika Antonova from the University of Cambridge's research focused on co-design, automated algorithm discovery, and data-efficient reinforcement learning in robotics.

The research involved developing methods to integrate artificial intelligence with physical robot systems by focusing on collaborative design and discovering optimal algorithms through automated means.
The methodology employed data-efficient reinforcement learning techniques to train these systems effectively, building upon prior experience from research environments such as Google.
This work advances the creation of more adaptable and intelligent robotic systems.
The ongoing research signals a progression toward more integrated and efficient autonomous machine development.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Hope you enjoyed diving into Skild AI's brainy robotics bet.
Until tomorrow, keep those algorithms humming!
